scope: Published the tested Streets 3073 compatibility and idle outfit-slot fixes. Experimental runtime Animation Studio remains local.

findings.pattern: Native function layout changes on every compared rebuild
findings.evidence: All 17 tracked native targets moved in each of five consecutive build transitions. Transitions had 16, 16, 10, 9 and 10 distinct address shifts, respectively.
findings.meaning: A single relocation offset is insufficient. Runtime already subtracts the module base, so ordinary ASLR is accounted for; these changes are to function layout inside new GameAssembly binaries.

findings.pattern: Generated coroutine names change when the game is recompiled
findings.evidence: Equipment iterator counters have changed from 80 to 111 to 112. Referencing a missing generated type directly can cause a type-load failure before a registrar's exception handler runs.
findings.accountedFor: The released registrar resolves supported names inside each feature group's error handling. The new metadata audit matches the owner/method/return/arguments exactly while allowing only the compiler-generated numeric iterator counter to differ. Multiple matches are rejected.

findings.evidence: LocalSpawnBullet changed from three arguments to four; RPC_FireBullet changed from three arguments to five.
findings.accountedFor: Known overloads are selected explicitly and compiled patch signatures are checked against installed wrappers. The new audit reports changed argument/return signatures as incompatible, including the available overloads, instead of selecting a similarly named function.

findings.pattern: Outfit completion and render state change independently of texture files
findings.evidence: A missing native completion hook prevented material application. In 3073, clearing an empty Hair/Eyes slot could leave its completion nonce unsettled even with no load in progress.
findings.accountedFor: 3.3.18 restores the audited completion hook and verifies that a slot is alive, empty, idle, has no pending request/coroutine/UID and has an invalid load handle before allowing the next request. It does not rewrite nonces or interrupt a real load.

findings.pattern: Compiler deduplication makes broad boolean getters unsafe hook targets
findings.evidence: The current common getter address has 504 metadata aliases, including otherwise unrelated tweak-state and prefab-completion getters.
findings.accountedFor: Hook ownership is audited across all assemblies and methods. The new tool rejects shared addresses and incomplete metadata inventories for the approved build.

newAudit.newBuildPreparation: Let MelonLoader regenerate matching interop wrappers and produce fresh Cpp2IL metadata from the updated GameAssembly before discovery. The report fingerprints its supplied metadata; it cannot independently prove that stale metadata was generated from a different binary.
outputs: candidate-native-profile.json when every target passes structural and ownership checks
checks: GameAssembly hash before and after scanning
Unique address ownership across all supplied metadata
Metadata hashes and changing file inventory
promotionProcedure: Review every reported native target and signature change; discovery never edits the approved runtime profile.
Add a reviewed build mapping and supported wrapper aliases as needed, retaining older supported profiles.
Run Scripts/Test-TrickTweakNativeTargets.ps1 and Scripts/Test-LateNativeHookRegistration.ps1 against the exact release DLL and current wrappers, plus compiled wrapper-reference checks.
Run native-registration and outfit regression tests, including legacy, current, missing-wrapper and unsupported-build cases.
Verify native hook groups, trick guards and outfit completion in game; distinguish that from physical-controller, multiplayer and replay acceptance.
Publish only the tested DLL and verify the downloaded release asset, updater DLL, manifest and website checksum.
newAudit.safety: Report-only discovery does not patch the game, replace wrappers or enable native hooks. Unknown game hashes remain unsupported by the runtime until a reviewed release. Metadata alone cannot verify changed gameplay semantics.

remainingLimits: The new audit shortens and standardizes future update triage. It cannot guarantee compatibility with arbitrary future native or gameplay changes.
Invalid material bundles, unreadable/custom mesh issues and stale individual preset material paths still require asset or preset corrections.
